findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies math.floor/ceil to datetime keys and crashes the audit log endpoint
findings.body:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` copies the integer `Paginator` implementation and runs `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`.

The only caller, `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`, uses `order_by="-datetime"`, so the value is a `datetime`. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`.

`build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])` whenever the page has results. So every `optimized_pagination=true` request that returns at least one row fails with a 500.

findings.title: Raw numeric cursor value used to filter a datetime column
findings.body:
`value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged. `build_queryset` then emits `WHERE datetime <= %s` with that integer or float.

`DateTimePaginator` instead converts the millisecond value back into a timezone-aware `datetime`. Here the integer is compared against a timestamp column, which either raises a database error or filters incorrectly.

Any cursor-based navigation of audit logs through the optimized path is therefore broken. The paginator should extend `DateTimePaginator` (or reuse its key/value conversion) when ordering by a datetime.

findings.title: Negative QuerySet slicing is unsupported in Django and raises an error
findings.body:
The "advanced" branch slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. The comment claims the ORM handles negative slicing automatically, but it does not: Django raises `ValueError`/`AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported").

A user-supplied cursor like `0:-5:0` therefore produces a 500 instead of a clean 400 `BadPaginationError`.

The comments also say this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" and is "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level". That rationale is misleading. Negative offsets should be rejected, as `OffsetPaginator` does.

findings.title: BasePaginator change silently clamps negative next offsets but passes negative prev offsets to the QuerySet
findings.body:
This change affects every `BasePaginator` subclass (`DateTimePaginator`, `Paginator`, etc.) used across the API.

- For forward cursors, a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0. But `build_cursor` still computes the next cursor from the original negative `cursor.offset`, so the returned next/prev cursors can be wrong (e.g. `offset + limit` stays negative or small).
- For `is_prev` cursors, the negative offset is still passed straight into `queryset[offset:stop]`, which errors.

The comment calling this "safe" is incorrect. Malformed cursors should be rejected with `BadPaginationError` rather than half-handled.

findings.title: Gate uses is_superuser rather than active superuser, and member may be None
findings.body:
`request.user.is_superuser` is true for superuser accounts even without an active superuser session. Sentry normally gates superuser-only behavior with `is_active_superuser(request)`, so this bypasses that convention.

Separately, for a non-superuser accessing via staff or other paths, `organization_context.member` can be `None`. In that case `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError` and the request returns a 500.

findings.title: New paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body:
The PR adds a new paginator, a new query parameter (`optimized_pagination`), and changes the core `BasePaginator.get_result` offset handling, all without tests.

A basic test of `optimized_pagination=true` for an org owner returning audit rows would have exposed the `TypeError` on datetime keys. A test with a negative-offset cursor would have exposed the unsupported negative slice.
